hook.text: Netflix streams stutter at 9 PM because everyone watches at once. That's network congestion—demand exceeds capacity.

buildup.text: When traffic exceeds a link's capacity, packets queue in buffers. Too much queueing causes delay and packet loss.

discovery.text: Little's law: average queue length equals arrival rate times average wait time. It governs every buffer in every router.

twist.text: TCP's congestion control backs off when it detects loss, then slowly increases again. It's a distributed negotiation.

climax.text: Congestion control is game theory: each sender maximizes throughput while competing for shared resources.

punchline.text: Too many packets, too little pipe. Congestion is the network's traffic jam.
